thread:
support-eng: Heads-up — customer (acme-corp) opened a P1: after we rolled the new quant profile last night (int8-calib-v2 -> enabled fp8 fallback), their /v1/generate p95/p99 jumped a lot for chat workloads with long histories. They say it started ~03:10 UTC. Full repro below.

maya: Ack, can you paste the exact request they used?

support-eng: Yep, here's the sanitized curl they used:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","quant_profile":"int8-calib-v2","context":[{"role":"user","content":"(~20 messages chat history)"}],"max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
```

support-eng: Observed numbers reported by customer (after profile flip): p50=120ms p95=430ms p99=1.25s. Baseline on fp16 yesterday: p50=90ms p95=160ms p99=420ms.

kevin: That looks like a perf regression with KV-cache / attention kernels under int8+fp8 fallback on long sequences. We saw similar noise in canary when fp8 path was enabled for certain seq len distributions.

ryan: Oncall: can we confirm if their requests hit a dedicated pool or hosted?

support-eng: Hosted. They are on the standard tier and we routed them to the new profile automatically.

maya: OK. Immediate mitigation options: 1) force-route the customer to the fp16 variant of the model (pin model_version or quant_profile) 2) disable fp8 fallback at routing level (runtime flag) 3) revert the quant profile rollout for that region.

kevin: For repro locally you can run our perf harness:
```
PYTHONPATH=./tools python perf/harness.py --model redwood-13b --profile int8-calib-v2 --sequence 1024 --clients 4 --batching on
```
We saw p99 blow up when sequence > 800 and microbatch merging interacts badly with the fp8 kernel selection.

maya: Quick checks we need from customer (or we can fetch traces): 1) sample request id(s) 2) region/edge 3) X-Model-Version header 4) whether they have streaming enabled 5) heap/throughput on their side.

support-eng: They gave two request ids: req_01G3 and req_01G4. Region us-east-1, not streaming. Model-Version header shows: redwood-13b@v2026-03-14-quant-int8-calib-v2

kevin: Thanks. I'll pull profiler traces for those req IDs and check kernel path selection and quant_dequant toggles. If we see frequent fallback to fp16 inside the call that could explain tail latency.

oncall-bot: Incident assigned to @maya and escalation channel created: #inc-2305012345. ETA initial triage 20m. :rotating_light:

maya: Quick mitigation I just pushed to routing: pin acme-corp to redwood-13b@v2026-03-14-fp16-locked for 2 hours and disabled fp8 fallback for that tenant. Please confirm if their p99 drops.

support-eng: Confirmed with customer — they report p95 now ~170ms p99 ~430ms. They say it feels back to normal.

kevin: From profiler for req_01G3 I see kernel transitions: int8-kernel -> fp8-dequantize -> slow attention fallback path -> occasional fallback to fp16 for softmax stability. The FP8 path has larger per-token variance on long KV-cache reuse because of quant calibration mismatch.

maya: Action plan:
- Stop global rollout of fp8-enabled profiles until we fix calibration heuristics.
- Add a route-level safety: if p99 exceeds baseline*2 for 5m, auto-pin to fp16 for that tenant.
- Add runtime flag to force no-fp8-inference (--runtime.quant.disable_fp8) and expose as tenant config.
- Create a regression test in perf harness for seq lengths 512/1024 with KV reuse.

ryan: Also recommend we add telemetry counters: count of "quant_fallback_ratio" per request and histogram of kernel switch counts. Right now it's hard to correlate fallback frequency to tail latency.

kevin: Will run calibration rework — adjust percentile used for scale factors (use 99.5th for activations in long context paths) and re-run on the calibration dataset. We'll push candidate profile int8-calib-v2b for internal canary.

sasha: From the customer's side: thanks, that pinned fix helped. They asked if we can make fallback automatic for only the heavy-history requests (they have a mixture).

maya: Yep — we can add an adaptive routing rule: if sequence_length_estimate > 600, prefer fp16 or the quant_profile with "no-fp8". That should reduce tail noise while keeping int8 for shorter calls.

support-eng: I'll follow up with acme and keep the ticket open; will collect any more failing request ids. Leaving incident open until rollback complete and calibrations validated.

kevin: I'll post the canary results here once int8-calib-v2b runs (ETA 3h).

maya: Thanks team. Filed follow-ups: ENG-RUNTIME-312 (telemetry + runtime flag), ENG-ML-198 (recalibration + test), OPS-455 (routing safety). Closing loop after canary.

support-eng: Closing note: temporary customer routing to fp16 is the immediate mitigation; long-term fix is improving calibration and adding sequence-aware routing.

ryan: 👍 keep monitoring.

oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2305012345 updated: status=investigating -> mitigated.
